en: O Sarasvatī, I bow to your pair of feet, which are praised by Ravi, Rudra, Pitāmaha, and Viṣṇu; which are smeared with the paste of yellow sandalwood and saffron; and which are attended by hosts of sages and lordly elephants. 1.

O Sarasvatī, I bow to your pair of feet, which possess the coolness of the moon’s pure nectar and snow, whose rays are equal to the orb of the autumnal sky, and which are endowed with the enchanting luster of many jewels. 2.

O Sarasvatī, I bow to your pair of feet, which are adorned with the splendor of golden lotuses; which transcend the state of worldly existence through the eloquent exposition of the nature of becoming; and which are the excellent path for the virtuous who are absorbed in the mind of the Lord. 3.

O Sarasvatī, I bow to this pair of your feet, which grant the state of stainless and primordial purity, and which bestow the lineage of practice for those terrified by sinking into the ocean of existence. 4.

O Sarasvatī, I bow to this pair of your feet, which provide refuge for those destitute of intellect; which consist of words spoken in all the scriptures yet distinct from one another; and which have fulfilled the manifold existences of the entire universe. (5)

O Sarasvatī, I bow to your pair of feet— the treasury that fulfills all desires, the storehouse of discernment through the investigation of ultimate truth, and the soles of whose feet are served by celestial nymphs.

O Sarasvatī, I bow to your pair of feet, which possess rays made white by the luster of the jewels on the crowns of the gods, which remove the fear of the great dangers such as the sense-objects, and which make even Śiva’s moon pale by their own radiance.

O Sarasvatī, I bow to your pair of feet, whose soles are as tender as the interior of a lotus; a state feared by those who stand alone in their virtues, yet a ground of truth made proud by the weight of its own qualities.
Whoever should recite this daily at the three junctions of the day, whether standing in water or on dry land, shall through mere recitation become wise and repeatedly established in Brahman.
This hymn of great merit was proclaimed by Brahmā;
Sarasvatī shall reside in the throat of whoever recites it upon rising in the morning.
